findings.locator: Berthe, La chute de la pratique catholique en France autour de 1965; accessible bibliographical abstract
findings.document_finding: This specific French scholarly article investigates the mid-1960s decline in Sunday observance, rather than declaring a universal single-cause explanation.
findings.qualification: Only bibliographic/abstract scope was accessible in this pass. Full statistical series and Cuchet's monograph are not certified; the causal question remains open.

findings.locator: Pius X, Pascendi, §§4–7: the composite Modernist system, agnosticism and religious immanence
findings.document_finding: Pius X explicitly reconstructs a connected set of philosophical and theological assertions, rather than condemning every use of the word change.
findings.qualification: A systematic doctrinal condemnation is not evidence that every conciliar change reproduces those propositions.

findings.locator: Sacrosanctum Concilium arts. 21–23 on general reform principles
findings.document_finding: The liturgical constitution sets forth reform norms including preserving sound tradition and making changes according to genuine need.
findings.qualification: The existence of conciliar reform prescriptions is not an original-document finding that Pius X's condemned propositions were adopted.

findings.locator: Dignitatis humanae §§1–2: duty toward true religion; immunity from civil coercion
findings.document_finding: The declaration expressly says the traditional moral duty of persons and societies toward true religion remains untouched while describing immunity from coercion.
findings.qualification: This formulation alone does not decide the full disputed relation to earlier civil duties.

findings.locator: Leo XIII, Libertas, later paragraphs on civil toleration
findings.document_finding: Leo XIII allows toleration of certain civil liberties for just reasons while refusing to treat religious error as a positive moral good.
findings.qualification: The distinction between toleration and an articulated civil right requires direct proposition-by-proposition comparison.

findings.locator: Francis, letter to bishops accompanying Traditionis custodes (16 July 2021), survey and unity reasons
findings.document_finding: Francis cites the episcopal questionnaire and claims that some liturgical attachments aggravated ecclesial division.
findings.qualification: The letter reports the legislator's reasons, not a full public dataset proving these descriptions about every community.

findings.locator: Ecclesia Dei superiors, Courtalain communiqué of 31 August 2021
findings.document_finding: The superiors explicitly deny claiming to be the only true Church and assert loyalty to the Pope and diocesan bishops.
findings.qualification: This is the communities' own documented response, not independent adjudication of every individual group's conduct.

findings.locator: DDF Italian decree, 2 July 2026, canons 1387 and 1364 §1; named bishops
findings.document_finding: The decree expressly declares six episcopal excommunications following the unauthorised consecrations, naming both consecrators and four new bishops.
findings.qualification: The decree's declarations must not be silently extended to all lay visitors or confused with the separate explanatory note.

findings.locator: DDF explanatory note, 2 July 2026, paragraphs on ministers, laity and sacraments
findings.document_finding: The note addresses ministers' status, invalidity of specified penance and marriage ministries, and conditional formal adherence by lay faithful.
findings.qualification: Individual lay culpability and the procedural consequences of recourse are not adjudicated by this general note.

findings.locator: 1983 Code, canon 1353, appeals against penalties
findings.document_finding: Canon 1353 attaches suspensive effect to an appeal or recourse against a judgement or decree imposing or declaring a penalty.
findings.qualification: A preliminary can.1734 petition is separately regulated by can.1736; applying both provisions to this precise act calls for canonical adjudication.

findings.locator: 1983 Code, canon 212 §§1–3, obedience and responsible expression
findings.document_finding: The canon binds the faithful to Christian obedience, permits needs to be expressed, and sometimes requires knowledgeable, reverent expression of opinions.
findings.qualification: Neither §1 nor §3 authorizes either blanket resistance or blanket dismissal of objections.

findings.locator: Aquinas, Summa II–II q.104 a.5, response and replies
findings.document_finding: Aquinas states two limits: a higher divine command and matters outside the superior's competence.
findings.qualification: Neither limit gives individuals a general exemption from legitimate orders they find imprudent.

findings.locator: 25 March 2020 Holy Week decree; limited 2020 extraordinary arrangements
findings.document_finding: The Congregation allowed specific Holy Week celebrations without assembled faithful in affected places and kept Easter on its fixed date.
findings.qualification: A universal rule that every religious act was forbidden, or that the Sunday obligation was abolished everywhere, does not follow.

findings.locator: Apostolic Penitentiary note of 20 March 2020 on confession
findings.document_finding: The Penitentiary maintained individual confession as ordinary and discussed general absolution only under danger of death or grave necessity.
findings.qualification: Emergency sacramental provisions and a bishop's concrete determination are not interchangeable with a general dispensation from sacramental care.

findings.locator: Canon 212 §3 conditions: knowledge, competence, prestige, reverence and persons' dignity
findings.document_finding: The canon expressly makes responsible expression conditional on competence and the integrity of faith, morals, reverence and persons' dignity.
findings.qualification: A right to express an opinion is not a right to issue unproved accusations or self-declared penalties.

findings.locator: Aquinas, Summa II–II q.33 a.4: charity and correction of a prelate
findings.document_finding: Aquinas distinguishes fraternal correction in charity from coercive correction by juridical superiority.
findings.qualification: His allowance for public correction in danger to the faith is not an assertion of lay power to depose a superior.

findings.locator: Canon 838, current post-Magnum principium wording
findings.document_finding: The Code assigns ordering and guidance of liturgy to the Church's authority, Apostolic See and bishops according to law.
findings.qualification: Competence to regulate sacred worship is not a general proposition that every exercise of that power is prudent or doctrinally irreformable.

findings.locator: 2021 accompanying letter and description of superseded permission
findings.document_finding: The letter states the reasons Francis gave for revising permissions originally widened under Summorum Pontificum.
findings.qualification: This legislative statement does not itself prove every older-form community repudiated the Council.

findings.locator: Rescriptum ex audientia of 20 February 2023, two reserved dispensation categories
findings.document_finding: The original rescript reserves parish-church/personal-parish dispensations and post-Traditionis-custodes priests' permissions to the Apostolic See.
findings.qualification: It does not purport to suppress every institute-specific faculty or create an undifferentiated blanket prohibition.

findings.locator: 2021 Responsa ad dubia, actual implementation rules
findings.document_finding: The Responsa provide detailed applications of Traditionis custodes under the Congregation's delegated authority.
findings.qualification: These instructions are not a free-standing legal repeal of every particular faculty held under other acts.

findings.locator: Novus Ordo Watch, 2015 critique of recognise-and-resist and named opposing writers
findings.document_finding: The sedevacantist author directly argues that recognising a purported pope while resisting a broad range of his alleged errors is incoherent.
findings.qualification: A real partisan argument has been located; its premises and validity remain contested, not independently certified.

findings.locator: Bellarmine, De Romano Pontifice II.30, Ryan Grant English translation of the fifth opinion
findings.document_finding: Bellarmine argues conditionally about a manifest heretic ceasing to be pope and distinguishes positions on how such loss happens.
findings.qualification: A debated theoretical conclusion does not itself prove that any contemporary person meets its factual or legal predicates.

findings.locator: Catechism §§2477–2479: rash judgment, detraction and calumny
findings.document_finding: The text distinguishes rash judgment, detraction and calumny and describes the duty to protect a person's good name.
findings.qualification: Firm public criticism of verified acts is not automatically slander; motives and allegations still require evidence.

findings.locator: Redemptionis sacramentum, 2004 instruction on abuses of the Eucharist
findings.document_finding: The instruction governs specified abuses in the Church's reformed liturgical discipline and prescribes corrective measures.
findings.qualification: The existence of a prohibition does not quantify its violation, nor does this instruction by itself codify the 1962 Missal's rubrics.

findings.locator: General Instruction of the Roman Missal, 2003 English typical edition norms
findings.document_finding: The GIRM supplies specific norms for celebrations according to the reformed Roman Missal.
findings.qualification: Do not impose these provisions unmodified upon an earlier book or use an isolated exception to invalidate the new rite wholesale.
